findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: The field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the module is imported. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` therefore carries the process start time, not the time it was queued, which makes the field meaningless. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: datetime in Celery task kwargs breaks JSON serialization
findings.body: `asdict()` keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object, and that dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` in the task kwargs. Sentry's Celery uses JSON serialization, which either cannot serialize the datetime or turns it into a string. In the string case, `from_dict` silently accepts a str for `queued`. In the failure case, enqueueing the task raises and the outbound sync is lost. Tests run under `self.tasks()`, which executes eagerly, so they do not catch this. Serialize `queued` explicitly (for example as ISO format or a timestamp) and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg passed to integrations that may not accept it
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)` on every integration. Any provider whose `sync_assignee_outbound` override (Jira, GitHub, VSTS, etc.) lacks `**kwargs` or an `assignment_source` parameter will raise TypeError, which breaks all outbound assignee sync for that provider. This PR does not update any of those implementations.

findings.title: Inbound status sync path does not use AssignmentSource
findings.body: Only assignee sync passes a source. Status changes coming in from an integration can still trigger outbound status sync back to the same integration, so the same cycle problem remains for status. Meanwhile the new `assignment_source` parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is never supplied by any caller.
